links.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of MRI reports versus GPT-4o layman explanations
links.effect: Mean FRES of MRI reports 32.15 (SD 15.89) vs GPT-4o explanations 53.9 (SD 7.86; P<.001); FKGL 11th-12th grade vs 10th-11th grade (P=.11), still above plain-language level.
links.quote: The mean FRES score of the MRI reports was significantly lower than the GPT-4o explanations (32.15, SD 15.89 vs 53.9, SD 7.86; P<.001).

links.outcome: Reading grade level of GPT-4o patient explanations versus source reports
links.effect: GPT-4o explanations remained at 10th-11th grade level (MRI reports 11th-12th grade; P=.11), above typical patient reading level.
links.quote: The mean FKGL score of the MRI reports trended higher compared to the GPT-4o explanations (11th-12th grade vs 10th-11th grade level; P=.11).

links.outcome: Spine surgeon ratings of accuracy of GPT-4o layman explanations
links.effect: All 7 surgeons rated accurate in 11/20 (55%); 6 of 7 in 5/20 (25%); 4 or 5 of 7 in 4/20 (20%).
links.quote: ChatGPT-generated layman reports were rated as "accurate" by all 7 surgeons in 11/20 cases (55%).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, helpfulness, and readability of GPT-4o-generated patient-facing explanations of spinal MRI reports evaluated by spine surgeons, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
